topicName: User Defined Functions (UDFs) and Pandas UDFs
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"User Defined Functions (UDFs) and Pandas UDFs in Apache Spark"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Apache Spark provides robust APIs for distributed data processing. However, built-in functions do not always cover complex custom business logic. To bridge this gap, Spark supports User Defined Functions (UDFs), allowing developers to write custom code in Python, Scala, or Java. This tutorial explores standard UDFs and high-performance Pandas UDFs (Vectorized UDFs)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Standard Spark UDFs"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Standard UDFs allow you to apply custom Python functions row by row to a Spark DataFrame. While flexible, they suffer from significant performance overhead because of serialization between the JVM and Python worker processes for every single row."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
from pyspark.sql.types import StringType

# Initialize Spark session
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName('UDF Tutorial').getOrCreate()

# Define a standard Python function
def categorize_age(age):
    if age < 18:
        return 'Minor'
    elif age < 65:
        return 'Adult'
    else:
        return 'Senior'

# Register the UDF
categorize_age_udf = udf(categorize_age, StringType())

# Sample DataFrame
data = [(15,), (30,), (70,)]
df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ['age'])

# Apply UDF
result_df = df.withColumn('category', categorize_age_udf(df['age']))
result_df.show()"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Pandas UDFs (Vectorized UDFs)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"To overcome the row-by-row performance bottleneck of standard UDFs, Apache Spark introduced Pandas UDFs. Powered by Apache Arrow, Pandas UDFs allow vectorized operations. Instead of processing one row at a time, data is transferred in batches as Pandas Series or Pandas DataFrames, offering orders of magnitude better performance."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
from pyspark.sql.functions import pandas_udf

# Define a Pandas UDF using Arrow vectorization
@pandas_udf('string')
def categorize_age_pandas(age: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    result = []
    for val in age:
        if val < 18:
            result.append('Minor')
        elif val < 65:
            result.append('Adult')
        else:
            result.append('Senior')
    return pd.Series(result)

# Apply Pandas UDF
result_pandas_df = df.withColumn('category_pandas', categorize_age_pandas(df['age']))
result_pandas_df.show()"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Differences and Best Practices"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Standard UDFs serialize data row-by-row, leading to high CPU overhead and slow execution on large datasets."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pandas UDFs leverage Apache Arrow for zero-copy data transfer, drastically minimizing serialization costs."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always prefer native Spark SQL built-in functions over UDFs when possible, as Spark's Catalyst Optimizer can optimize native functions much more effectively."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Pandas UDFs when complex Python logic cannot be expressed using native Spark functions."}]
